diagnostic_evidence.quote: We will also show that, under specific domain decomposition parameters, in addition to scalability, the one-level Schwarz method can also achieve robustness with respect of the wavenumber.

Finally in \Cref{sec:numeric} we present two types of numerical results: first, showing that the limiting spectrum is descriptive for the convergence of the algorithm even in the case of a moderate number of domains and then on the discretised problem using the edge element method.
Secondly, we aim at showing scalability for discretised Maxwell's equation in a waveguide and decomposition into many subdomains when using different types of transmission conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract, introduction, and Section 4 explicitly claim that the paper demonstrates that the one-level Schwarz method achieves robustness with respect to the wavenumber under specific domain decomposition parameters, and that numerical scalability results are presented for discretized Maxwell equations using the edge element method. However, the paper contains no analysis, parameter scaling, proof, or numerical experiments addressing wavenumber robustness (all numerical tests evaluate fixed wavenumber k = 10 or k = 10 + i). Moreover, Section 4 contains only Section 4.1 on the continuous modal limiting spectrum; no discrete formulation, edge element method, or discretized scalability experiments appear anywhere in the paper.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, we demonstrate that the one-level Schwarz method can achieve robustness with respect to the wave number under specific domain decomposition parameters, offering new insights into its applicability for large-scale electromagnetic wave problems.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either provide the complete mathematical analysis and numerical experiments establishing wavenumber robustness and discrete edge element scalability, or withdraw the advertised wavenumber robustness guarantee and edge element claims from the abstract, introduction, and Section 4.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantees regarding wavenumber robustness and the advertised computational validation of the method on discretized Maxwell systems using edge elements are completely unsupported.
issues.title: Unsupported claims of wavenumber robustness and discretized edge element scalability
issues.why_classification: Wavenumber robustness is advertised as a major contribution and capability of the method in the abstract and introduction. Resolving the defect requires either developing entirely new theoretical and numerical proof architecture establishing this guarantee or abandoning a central advertised property of the solver.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\lambda_i^{\rm TE} = -\beta^{\rm TE}_i$, $\lambda^{\rm TM}_i = -\frac{k^2}{\beta^{\rm TM}_i}$ and $\lambda^{\rm TEM}_i = -\imath k$. Therefore, this clearly leads to $a^{\rm T}_i = 0$ in the definition of $a^{\rm T}_i$ given in \cref{prop:R-ite} because $\kappa = \lambda^{\rm T}_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition 3.7 and its proof state that for an infinite PML (ell = +\infty), lambda_i^T = kappa, which is then used to evaluate b_i^T. However, according to (3.10) and Proposition 3.5, the transparent PML limit gives lambda_i^TE = -i beta_i^TE = -kappa, lambda_i^TEM = -i k = -kappa, and lambda_i^TM = -i k^2 / beta_i^TM = -kappa. Thus lambda_i^T = -kappa, not kappa. Substituting lambda_i^T = -kappa into the definition of b_i^T(kappa) from Proposition 3.5 yields b_i^T = e^{+i beta_i^T (L+delta)}, whereas the source has e^{-i beta_i^T (L+delta)}. For evanescent modes (where Im(beta_i^T) > 0), the source's formula yields an exponentially growing quantity e^{+|Im(beta)|(L+delta)} across iterations rather than an exponentially decaying factor.

failure_location.quote: we have $\lambda^{\rm T}_i = \kappa$ and therefore $a^{\rm T}_i = 0$ and $b^{\rm T}_i = e^{-\imath \beta^{\rm T}_i (L+\delta)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the relation to lambda_i^T = -kappa, include the factor i in the limits in the proof, and correct the resulting coefficient to b_i^T = e^{+i beta_i^T (L+delta)}.
issues.overall_effect: The stated coefficient b_i^T in Proposition 3.7 has the wrong sign in the exponent, incorrectly implying exponential error blow-up for evanescent modes under transparent boundary conditions. The nilpotency claim [I^T(i)]^N = 0 remains valid because a_i^T = 0 still holds when lambda_i^T = -kappa.
issues.title: Incorrect transmission parameter and exponential factor for transparent PML in Proposition 3.7
issues.why_classification: A routine local algebraic correction of the sign of lambda and the exponent of b preserves every substantive claim of Proposition 3.7, including a_i^T = 0 and the nilpotency property [I^T(i)]^N = 0.
